sections.h2: Which Mitchell County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two departments in Bakersville share the job. The Tax Assessor lists, appraises and assesses real and personal property, and the Tax Collector bills and takes payment. Both keep hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

  • Tax Assessor: 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 5, Bakersville, NC 28705, phone 828.688.2139 extension 1407.
  • Tax Collector: 61 Crimson Laurel Circle, Bakersville, NC 28705, phone 828.537.1627.

The assessor also administers applications for tax relief, exemption, exclusion and Present Use Value, the farm and forest program. The collector's bill covers fire tax for seven fire districts, so the line items on your bill depend on where the house sits.

sections.h2: What is Mitchell County like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Mitchell County is a small county. The Census Bureau estimated 15,062 residents on July 1, 2025, living on 221.25 square miles of land, which works out to about 67 people per square mile in 2020. The 2020 Census count was 14,903, down from 15,579 in 2010.

Most homes are owner-occupied. The 2020 to 2024 figures show a 76.3 percent owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $220,100 and 6,587 households. Median gross rent was $813. Residents aged 65 and over make up 27.6 percent of the population, and the mean commute is 24.4 minutes. Only 44 building permits were counted for 2025.

That age profile makes the state's elderly and disabled relief programs, described below, relevant to a large share of local owners.

sections.h2: When are Mitchell County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1, the last day to pay without interest is January 5, and January 6 is delinquent. Interest starts at 2 percent for the first month and adds three quarters of one percent each month after that. If a date falls on a weekend, it moves to the next business day.

Mitchell County tax calendar published by the Tax Collector
WhenWhat the office says

September 1Taxes become due and payable

The statewide rule behind the January 5 cutoff is G.S. 105-360.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Mitchell County tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay at the Tax Office by cash, check, debit card or credit card. Online payment by card or electronic check runs through mitchell.webtaxpay.com, and a third-party vendor adds a convenience fee.

The office also allows monthly installments on current-year taxes. Delinquent taxes can be paid in installments too, but only under a signed payment agreement. Anyone behind on a bill should call 828.537.1627 before the advertising step in March.

The county's own reminder is useful for sellers: bills go to the owner of record as of January 1, so you should check the attorney's closing papers to confirm the tax obligation has been settled. If a house changed hands during the year, the bill can still arrive in the previous owner's name.

sections.h2: What do I have to list with the Mitchell County assessor each January?
sections.html:
Any change to taxable real or personal property must be listed during January, the regular listing period under G.S. 105-307. The Board of County Commissioners can extend that window. The assessor warns that anyone who misses the regular period faces a 10 percent penalty.

Taxable personal property named on the assessor's page includes:

  • business assets,
  • untagged motor vehicles,
  • boats and personal watercraft,
  • untagged campers and trailers,
  • mobile homes,
  • aircraft.

Forms are printed, filled out and mailed to the Tax Assessor at the Suite 5 address. Current versions come from the North Carolina Department of Revenue. A new addition, a demolished outbuilding or a placed manufactured home are all changes worth reporting during that month.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Mitchell County property value?
sections.html:
Appeal to the county Board of Equalization and Review, which is made up of the commissioners unless a special board exists. It first meets no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May, under G.S. 105-322.

  • Ask for a hearing in writing or in person before the board adjourns.
  • If the notice of a decision went out fewer than 15 days before adjournment, you have 15 days from the mailing.
  • The board mails its decision within 30 days after it adjourns.
  • A further appeal to the Property Tax Commission is filed within 30 days after the board mailed notice (G.S. 105-290).

State law requires reappraisal of real property at least every eighth year. Ask the assessor which year your parcel was last reappraised and when the next is scheduled, because in a revaluation year the board runs until December 1.

sections.h2: What if I fall behind on Mitchell County taxes before I sell?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax carries a lien on the parcel, and the county can enforce it in court. Under G.S. 105-355 the lien attaches as of the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs attach with it. A foreclosure action under G.S. 105-374 is filed in the county where the land lies and leads to a public sale at the courthouse door.

That sale is not instant. The commissioner reports it within three days, and anyone may file an increased bid or an exception within 10 days of the report. Before the sale is confirmed, a person redeeming the property pays the taxes plus penalties, interest and costs. A seller who closes before the sale date keeps control of the price.

The practical order for a Mitchell County seller is short. Get a payoff from the Tax Collector, ask the Tax Assessor whether a relief application or deferral is on the parcel, and give both figures to the closing attorney.

sections.h2: What tax relief can a Mitchell County owner claim?
sections.html:
Three state programs exist and an owner can receive only one. The elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value, for owners 65 or older or permanently disabled with income at or below $38,800 for 2026. The disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of value, with no age or income cap. The circuit breaker limits tax to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for income up to 150 percent of the limit, which is $58,200 for 2026.

All three use Form AV-9 filed with the Mitchell County Tax Assessor, who administers relief applications locally. A new application is needed each year for the circuit breaker. Deferred circuit breaker tax becomes due when the owner sells or stops living in the home, so sellers should ask the assessor for the deferred balance before closing. The rules are in G.S. 105-277.1B.

If you inherited a Mitchell County house with back taxes and no plan to keep it, a cash sale can settle the balance without repairs or showings.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Mitchell County property tax without interest?
faqs.a: January 5. Taxes become due September 1, and they turn delinquent on January 6, when 2 percent interest starts. Three quarters of one percent more is added for each later month.

faqs.q: Where is the Mitchell County Tax Collector's office?
faqs.a: It is at 61 Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone number is 828.537.1627.

faqs.q: Who do I contact to change my property record or ask about relief?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor, at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 5, Bakersville, phone 828.688.2139 extension 1407. That office lists, appraises and assesses property and handles exemption, exclusion and Present Use Value applications.

faqs.q: Can I pay Mitchell County taxes in monthly installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Office accepts monthly installments on current-year taxes. Delinquent taxes can also be paid that way if you sign a payment agreement.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for failing to list property in January?
faqs.a: Yes, a 10 percent penalty applies to property not listed during the regular listing period, according to the assessor. The period is the month of January unless the commissioners extend it.
